$comment: Inverted truthfulness check. A page can contain no false sentence and still mislead by omitting a limitation we know exists. Every entry must cite verifiedBy: how we know the limitation is real. Never add an entry from memory alone.

caveats.why: Safari support is macOS only, needs full Xcode, and has no live reload. A reader who skips this ships a broken dev loop.
caveats.verifiedBy: extension build --help: 'safari builds a Safari app via Xcode (macOS only)'; docs/browsers/safari.mdx already states it, this entry keeps it from being dropped; translations verified 2026-08-22 (zh-Hans line 24 and 108, zh-Hant line 25 both carry the no-live-reload limit)

caveats.why: content_scripts[].world is a Chromium MV3 field. The Firefox MV2 build keeps the key, and Firefox ignores it, so a MAIN world script silently runs in the isolated world instead.
caveats.verifiedBy: programs/develop/plugin-web-extension/feature-manifest/manifest-overrides/common/content_scripts.ts:20 comment 'Chromium-only (MV3+) field'; built examples/content-main-world dist/firefox/manifest.json is manifest_version 2 and still carries world: MAIN

anyOf: headless[^\n]{0,60}(extensions are not|does not support|drops|will not load)
caveats.why: The page's example sets headless: false with no explanation. Playwright's default headless mode runs headless_shell, which silently loads no extensions, so a reader adapting the snippet for CI gets a green run that tested nothing.
caveats.verifiedBy: Playwright chromium headless_shell does not support extensions; verified in this project while building the visual-render and reload suites, which require headless: false plus --headless=new
